reviewerRole: Independent reader of root-owned flow/application integration, Backend/storage and worker fence. Prior self-produced Controller/Preview implementation is excluded from an independent security PASS.

observedFacts.fact: The memory-only cancellation/deadline/stop/fault fence is checked alongside the exact existing Manage session guard at writer evaluation and precommit. False or panic is mapped to ProfileContent Expired; the fence grants no actor/administration authority.

The preparation/source owner closure exits before reservation settlement. This storage path uses blocking receiver recv rather than an early deadline-only caller wait. Reserved bytes cannot be safely settled merely because cancellation was requested.

COMMIT receipt carries the committed snapshot/digest. Fail changes only Accepted receipts. Settle changes only Reserved rows; Referenced originals remain referenced. A late cancellation or unknown delivery cannot roll back a completed COMMIT. User must reopen/read the original command outcome; this review does not claim all post-COMMIT returns are known success.

Runtime GC selects only Unreferenced/Retiring entries, CAS-retires, physically removes the controlled original, and only then finalizes quota release. Busy/error removal retains the charge and is retried. Runtime maintenance never age-settles Reserved; restart settlement is a separate exclusive handoff API.

Deleting a content node atomically removes its current/previous/pending head references and immutable versions, retires the head, and updates media references. Current plus Undo references protect originals. App schedules maintenance independently of a subsequent publication.

App owns a single Arc<Mutex<GcCursor>> reused across worker submissions. A physical job reads at most one 128-entry page. Completed entry attempts advance the typed cursor without holding its lock across SQL/FS. next_after requests a 1-second continuation; the end including an empty tail wraps to None. Cancelled/completion-discarded jobs retain already published cursor progress. App retains the ticket while try_result is None and cannot start a second maintenance job.

findings.classification: source-level liveness counterexample, not a runtime failure
findings.before: Each maintenance call restarted after=None. A repeated deadline or contention after a fixed prefix could forever leave later registry entries unseen even while retries continued. Returning a cursor only via Outcome would also lose progress when deadline handling discards the result.
findings.resolution: Root added App-owned durable-in-process shared cursor and one-page scanning; source implementation inspected above. Positive progress survives discarded outcomes. A busy failed entry can advance and is revisited after wraparound.
findings.oldSourceHash: No pre-fix file snapshot was independently captured; retain this as the observed pre-fix code/counterexample, not a claimed SHA-bound runtime reproduction.
findings.remainingLimit: No hard real-time or unconditional liveness proof: synchronous SQL/FS can run beyond the cooperative deadline; if every attempt expires before it can safely publish cursor progress, progress is not guaranteed. The implementation preserves ownership/quota and retries, rather than claiming physical interruption.
